title: Research Associate, Analytical Development
desc: About GenScript Founded in 2002 in New Jersey, GenScript Biotech Corporation accelerates innovation in biotech and healthcare by providing researchers and companies with the building blocks needed to develop groundbreaking treatments and products. Guided by its mission to Make People and Nature Healthier Through Biotechnology, and its role as a well-recognized biotechnology company, GenScript has a team of approximately 6,165 employees and has served more than 200,000 customers across over 100 countries and regions. Position Summary GenScript is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Research Associate, Analytical Development to support the development, qualification, and routine execution of analytical methods for RNA, lipids, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), and related bioconjugates at our Seattle site. The successful candidate will perform hands-on laboratory work across HPLC/UHPLC, LC-MS, nano flow cytometry, and RNA/LNP analytical testing. This role will support routine sample analysis, analytical method development and optimization, troubleshooting, and method transfer in close collaboration with R&D, QC, Production, and other cross-functional teams. This position is well suited for a scientist who combines strong wet-lab skills with attention to detail, analytical thinking, and a desire to build technical expertise in emerging RNA and lipid nanoparticle technologies. Key Responsibilities 1. Chromatography and Analytical Testing Prepare RNA, oligonucleotide, lipid, LNP, antibody, and bioconjugate samples for analytical testing according to established procedures and experimental plans. Perform HPLC/UHPLC analyses using UV and/or charged aerosol detection (CAD), including sample and standard preparation, instrument sequence setup, chromatogram review, peak integration, and initial data assessment. Support chromatographic methods for evaluating RNA purity, lipid identity and purity, lipid composition, residual components, and related product-quality attributes. Assist with preparative chromatography, fraction collection, sample tracking, and evaluation of purification fractions for RNA and related development projects. Support analytical method development, optimization, troubleshooting, and transfer under the guidance of senior scientists and the group lead. 2. LC-MS Characterization Support LC-MS characterization of RNA, oligonucleotides, synthetic cap analogs, and related materials. Assist with characterization of attributes such as molecular identity, capping efficiency, and poly(A) characteristics, as appropriate to the method and project. Perform sample preparation and assist with spectral review, data processing, and interpretation under scientific guidance. Support troubleshooting of sample-preparation, chromatographic, mass-spectrometric, and data-processing issues. 3. RNA and LNP Analytical Development Perform analytical testing to support characterization of mRNA, circRNA, oligonucleotides, lipids, LNPs, antibodies, and related bioconjugates, depending on project needs. Support assays evaluating RNA attributes such as concentration, purity, integrity/fragmentation, aggregation, and residual process-related components. Support characterization of LNP-related attributes, including lipid composition and purity and residual/free components associated with LNP conjugation or formulation processes. Perform routine sample cleanup, dilution, buffer preparation, and analytical sample processing using appropriate RNase-free techniques. 4. Nano Flow Cytometry and Targeted LNP Characterization Prepare fluorescently labeled samples, standards, and appropriate experimental controls for flow-cytometry analysis. Perform routine flow cytometer setup, instrument QC, sample acquisition, and application of established analysis and gating strategies. Support characterization of antibody-decorated or targeted LNPs, including evaluation of labeling and conjugation-related attributes where appropriate. Assist with optimization and troubleshooting of flow-cytometry-based analytical workflows. 5. Laboratory Execution and Data Analysis Perform routine wet-lab activities requiring accurate pipetting, serial dilution, buffer and reagent preparation, concentration measurements, and sample cleanup. Process analytical results using relevant instrument software and Microsoft Excel or equivalent data-analysis tools. Review results for consistency and data quality, prepare clear data summaries, and promptly communicate unexpected findings, deviations, or instrument issues to the group lead. Maintain accurate, complete, and traceable experimental documentation, sample records, reagent inventories, and laboratory records. 6. Laboratory Operations and Cross-Functional Support Support preparation and revision of SOPs, test methods, work instructions, and analytical documentation. Assist with routine instrument maintenance, laboratory organization, and method-transfer activities. Collaborate effectively with scientists and colleagues across R&D, QC, Production, and related functional teams. Follow applicable laboratory safety procedures, chemical-handling requirements, and site EHS policies. Contribute to continuous improvement of analytical workflows, laboratory efficiency, data quality, and technical capabilities. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Biotechnology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline. 0-5 years of relevant academic or industry laboratory experience, preferably in analytical chemistry, biopharmaceutical characterization, nucleic acid analysis, or a related field. Hands-on experience with HPLC/UHPLC and/or LC-MS, including sample preparation, execution of established analytical methods, and basic chromatographic or analytical data review. Practical experience with flow cytometry, including fluorescent sample preparation, use of appropriate controls, data acquisition, and basic gating or data interpretation. Strong fundamental wet-lab skills, including accurate pipetting, solution and buffer preparation, dilution calculations, sample handling, and contamination control. Ability to follow written procedures and experimental protocols accurately and maintain clear, complete, and traceable laboratory records. Ability to use Microsoft Excel or similar software to organize, analyze, and summarize experimental data. Strong attention to detail, organization, problem-solving ability, and willingness to learn new analytical technologies. Ability to manage multiple sample batches and experimental priorities while communicating progress, results, and technical issues clearly. Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary R&D environment. Preferred Qualifications Master's degree in Analytical Chemistry, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related discipline. Previous experience working with mRNA, circRNA, oligonucleotides, lipids, LNPs, antibodies, or bioconjugates. [...]

title: Machine Learning Scientist, Frontier Research, AI for Drug Discovery (AIDD)
desc: A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche. Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. Roche’s Research and Early Development organisations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. Seamless data sharing and access to models across gRED and pRED are essential to maximising these opportunities. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness the transformative power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist our scientists in both pRED and gRED to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide. ​ The Opportunity Within AI for Drug Discovery, the Frontier Research team advances fundamental machine learning and statistics methods, motivated by real-world challenges in drug discovery. In biology and medicine, many important problems cannot yet be addressed with off-the-shelf machine learning approaches—they demand not only novel solutions, but also new paradigms for framing and thinking about the problems themselves. Instead of focusing on incremental improvements, we work on long-horizon ideas that require a creative and broad perspective, developing solutions at a level that can be instantiated for multiple internal and external applications. If you’re excited about this kind of research, join us on an impactful journey of innovation at Prescient. In this role, you will: You will develop new methods and frameworks for uncertainty quantification, statistical inference, and experimental design, motivated by the diverse problem settings that arise when using machine learning to guide decision-making across the drug-discovery pipeline. You are expected to contribute to and drive research projects that result in conference and/or journal publications and open-source code, and that foster cross-organizational collaborations and applications. You are expected to engage actively in knowledge dissemination, presenting your work & expertise at internal and external scientific conferences. You will collaborate closely with our team in South San Francisco, New York, and Basel, Switzerland. Who You Are Must be pursuing, or have completed within the last 12 months, a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Computational Biology, or related technical field, or have demonstrated equivalent research productivity. Demonstrated expertise in (any paradigm of) uncertainty quantification for decision-making, e.g., sequential/online statistical inference, experimental design, conformal prediction, reinforcement learning, calibration, game-theoretic statistics, etc. Proven publication record and experience contributing to the research community, including at conferences like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AISTATS, UAI, etc., and/or relevant journals. Excellent skills in technical writing & communication, as well as collaboration and interpersonal skills. Preferred Experience with developing machine learning and/or statistical methods for biological/clinical data is desired, but not necessary. Experience developing open-source packages preferred. Relocation benefits are NOT available for this job posting The expected salary range for this position, based on the primary location of California, is $147,600 - 274,000. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below. Benefits #ComputationCoE #tech4lifeComputationalScience #tech4lifeAI Genentech

title: AI Scientist - Agentic Engineering
location: Paris France Linz Munich London Berlin remote
desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



The Role

Mistral AI is looking for AI Scientists with deep machine learning expertise and hands-on engineering experience to expand what Mistral's agentic tools can do across the engineering lifecycle across CAE (CFD, FEA etc) and EDA/Semi.. 

Within AI4Engineering Science, your core work is building the pre and post-training data for Mistral's LLMs to reason about and execute real engineering tasks. Alongside this, you'll help shape the agent architectures and harness that let these models operate reliably inside multi-step engineering workflows, not just answer isolated questions.

You'll work closely with domain experts across CAE and EDA to ground this work in how engineers actually work, and with the broader research team to translate that domain grounding into training signal and evaluation benchmarks that measure genuine task competence.

What You Will Do

 - Design pretraining, SFT, and RL data for engineering tasks across CAD, CAE, and semiconductor/EDA

 - Define verifiers and evaluation criteria that capture what "correct" and "high-quality" actually mean for each engineering task, beyond surface-level plausibility

 - Design and improve agent architectures and harnesses: how models plan, call tools, recover from errors, and chain steps together across long-horizon engineering workflows

 - Build evaluation benchmarks and diagnostic tooling to identify where models fail on engineering tasks, and trace those failures back to gaps in data, reward design, or agent scaffolding

 - Collaborate with domain experts across CAEand EDA (and the science and solutions teams more broadly) to identify which engineering workflows are highest-value to target next

 - Contribute to Mistral's broader pre and post-training research, sharing findings and methodology across the science organization

What We're Looking For

 - Fluent English with excellent communication skills, able to explain technical ML and engineering concepts to both engineering and non-technical audiences

 - Deep, hands-on machine learning expertise, particularly LLM development

 - Demonstrated experience running, debugging, and validating real engineering workflows in at least one of CAD, CAE, semiconductor simulation, or EDA. 

 - You write clean, readable Python code and are comfortable in Linux/HPC environments

 - Self-directed, you don't need detailed roadmaps to make progress

 - Low-ego, collaborative, and eager to learn at the intersection of engineering and ML

It would be great if you

 - Have experience building or fine-tuning agentic systems (tool use, multi-step planning, agent orchestration frameworks)

 - Have experience with reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF/RLVR, or preference-based training

 - Have industrial or academic experience with CAE, or EDA tools (e.g. SolidWorks, CATIA, Fluent, Abaqus, LS-DYNA, STAR-CCM+, Cadence/Synopsys/Siemens EDA tools)

 - Have contributed to a large open-source or industry codebase

 - Have publications in engineering and ML venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, JFM, AIAA, etc.)

 




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.




PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

title: Research Scientist, Modeling of Readout and Reset, Quantum
location: Goleta, CA, USA ; Los Angeles, CA, USA
desc: As an organization, Google maintains a portfolio of research projects driven by fundamental research, new product innovation, product contribution and infrastructure goals, while providing individuals and teams the freedom to emphasize specific types of work. As a Research Scientist, you'll setup large-scale tests and deploy promising ideas quickly and broadly, managing deadlines and deliverables while applying the latest theories to develop new and improved products, processes, or technologies. From creating experiments and prototyping implementations to designing new architectures, our research scientists work on real-world problems that span the breadth of computer science, such as machine (and deep) learning, data mining, natural language processing, hardware and software performance analysis, improving compilers for mobile platforms, as well as core search and much more. As a Research Scientist, you'll also actively contribute to the wider research community by sharing and publishing your findings, with ideas inspired by internal projects as well as from collaborations with research programs at partner universities and technical institutes all over the world. Google Quantum AI's goal is to build a practically useful quantum computer. Modeling of readout and reset team aims at quantitative understanding of error mechanisms of these operations, resulting in operation improvement and development of new schemes with advanced performance. Google Quantum AI is building quantum computing for otherwise unsolvable problems. The full potential of quantum computing will be unlocked with a large-scale computer capable of complex, error-corrected computations. Our roadmap is focused on advancing the capabilities of quantum computing and enabling meaningful applications. Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits Learn more about benefits at Google . Develop models for readout and reset in superconducting qubits, including numerical models of physical processes causing errors. Validate models with experimental results for system optimization and design. Collaborate closely with the hardware team to analyze and theoretically understand experimental data. Develop and maintain software and integrate it with data-taking infrastructure. Propose and analyze prospective readout and reset schemes with advanced performance. Minimum qualifications: PhD degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Experience with modeling of qubit systems. Experience in programming using Python. One of more scientific publication submission(s) for conferences, journals, or public repositories related to Quantum computing. Preferred qualifications: Experience with modeling superconducting qubit operations, particularly readout and reset. Experience with numerical simulations of quantum systems and with high-performance computing tools. Experience collaborating with experimentalists on quantum computing projects or analyzing/modeling experimental data. Experience with microwave engineering of superconducting qubits. Experience with error correction codes. Familiarity with circuit Quantum Electrodynamics (cQED). PhD degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Experience with modeling of qubit systems. Experience in programming using Python. One of more scientific publication submission(s) for conferences, journals, or public repositories related to Quantum computing.
